# TerraField Atlas

> Mission console for agricultural resilience and fire context using NASA POWER, GIBS, EONET and FIRMS. Missing observations remain missing. Globe stations/orbits are illustrative; reported events are polled, not instantaneous. Quantitative Earthdata science ingestion requires separate credentials.

TerraField Atlas is a Next.js mission console that answers six operator questions — observed conditions, how they changed, whether the changes are statistically meaningful, which crop rotations fit the evidence, how alternatives compare, and what the limits are — plus a full fire-intelligence module: VIIRS 375 m thermal-anomaly detections, regional watchlists on real scheduler cadences, cadence-aware digests, and signed push delivery.

## Key facts

- [Open API root](/api/v1/system/status): live system status — engines, providers, scheduler, digest channel, delivery exits, A/B experiments.
- [Health probe](/api/v1/health): liveness with per-source operational states.
- [Readiness probe](/api/v1/readyz): dependency checks.
- [Fire watchlists](/api/v1/fires/watchlists): regional watchlists, runs history, cadence-aware digests.
- [Curated demo regions](/api/v1/regions): 19 real agricultural regions with real coordinates (curated presets, not administrative boundaries).
- [Experiments API](/api/v1/experiments): deterministic A/B assignment + outcome ledger (no PII).
- [Sitemap](/sitemap.xml): crawlable URL list.
- [Module reference](/about): ten server-rendered module guides, methodology and privacy.
- [Recent FIRMS](/api/v1/fires/recent?lat=31&lon=-89): latest provider 24-hour product, separate from historical GIBS coverage.
- [Accounts](/account): verified email/password accounts for private farm, manual soil, rotation and report records; public-demo callsigns are not authentication.

## Deployment limits

- Google sign-in remains disabled until its OAuth client authorizes the TerraField callback.
- Private provider ingestion, analysis, scheduling and global digest exits are gated pending isolated storage and per-account destinations.
- Resend delivery is verified to the reserved `delivered@resend.dev` test inbox only. The configured signed webhook persists an idempotent local receipt; no external forwarding destination is configured.
- SoilGrids latency and satellite archive gaps remain upstream limitations. Shared request logs/job details are withheld from public responses for privacy; operational logging remains server-side.

## Principles

1. Source attribution: stored historical records and recent provider snapshots are distinguished; illustrative globe elements are labeled.
2. Honest gaps: archive gaps render as no-data with a stated reason — never zero-filled, never imputed.
3. Statistical rigor: Seasonal Mann-Kendall + Theil-Sen with autocorrelation correction and FDR control; ≥8 full years before any significance claim.
4. Provenance: retrieval attempts are logged server-side with credential redaction; unattributed diagnostics are not exposed across private accounts.
5. Delivery: configured public-demo exits are audited; configuration is not proof of delivery to a real user inbox.

## Statistical methodology (summary)

Monthly aggregation of complete months (≥20 valid days); Seasonal Mann-Kendall (Hirsch-Slack) with tie-corrected variance; Theil-Sen seasonal slope with Sen-rank 95% CI; Hamed-Rao lag-1 variance inflation when deseasonalized autocorrelation exceeds ±2/√n; Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across variables; ≥8 full years required before any significance claim.
